I now have a complete picture of the staged changes and surrounding context. Here is my structured review.

---

## Critical

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-bench-2026-05-23_v0.10.0-cold-post-trim/T1__leveraged__r2/work/service/routes/users.py:16`** — SQL injection via unsanitized f-string query

What: `user_id` is taken directly from `request.query` and interpolated into an SQL string with an f-string: `f"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = '{user_id}'"`. Any value like `' OR '1'='1` or `'; DROP TABLE users; --` is executed verbatim.

Why: This is a textbook SQL injection vulnerability. An unauthenticated-or-authenticated caller can read arbitrary rows, corrupt, or destroy data. The `@require_auth` decorator only verifies an `Authorization` header is present — it does not validate the token's value — so the bar to reach this code is trivially low.

Suggested direction: Use a parameterized query: pass the value as a positional parameter to `cursor.execute()` (`WHERE id = ?`, `(user_id,)`) instead of string interpolation. The repo already ships `service/validator.py` with `is_valid_id()` for exactly this kind of input; that should also be applied here as a defence-in-depth gate before the query runs.

---

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData\Local\Temp\leverage-bench-2026-05-23_v0.10.0-cold-post-trim\T1__leveraged__r2\work\service\routes\users.py:14`** — Missing input validation / unhandled `None` from query string

What: `request.query.get("id")` returns `None` when the `id` parameter is absent. That `None` is then formatted into the SQL string as the literal string `'None'`, producing a silently wrong query rather than a client error.

Why: The handler never checks whether `user_id` is present or valid before using it. The 404 branch is reached accidentally rather than intentionally, and other code paths (e.g., after the SQL injection fix with parameterized queries) would raise a `TypeError` or `InterfaceError` at runtime instead of returning a clean 400. `is_valid_id()` in the staged `validator.py` already handles the `None` case and would return `False`, so there is a purpose-built tool available that is simply not wired in.

Suggested direction: Call `is_valid_id(user_id)` immediately after reading from the query dict and return a 400 response if it fails, before any database interaction.

---

## Important

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData\Local\Temp\leverage-bench-2026-05-23_v0.10.0-cold-post-trim\T1__leveraged__r2\work\service\routes\users.py:7`** — Module-level shared mutable `sqlite3` connection is not thread-safe

What: `_DB = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")` is created once at import time and shared across all requests. `sqlite3` connections are not thread-safe by default (`check_same_thread=True` is the default, which would raise an error; here `:memory:` with `check_same_thread=False` not set means concurrent requests will either error or corrupt state depending on the WSGI/ASGI server's threading model).

Why: Under any multi-threaded server this will either raise `ProgrammingError: SQLite objects created in a thread can only be used in that same thread` or silently produce incorrect results. Even for a test fixture, establishing this as the pattern risks it being copied to production database code.

Suggested direction: Either use `check_same_thread=False` with a threading lock around executions, use `threading.local()` for per-thread connections, or (preferred for production code) move to a proper connection-pool pattern consistent with how the rest of the service manages persistence.

---

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData\Local\Temp\leverage-bench-2026-05-23_v0.10.0-cold-post-trim\T1__leveraged__r2\work\tests\test_users.py`** — No test coverage for the validation / bad-input paths

What: The new `validator.py` module and the `get_user` handler's error paths (missing `id` param, invalid `id` format, unknown user returning 404) have zero test coverage in the staged test file.

Why: The two existing tests only cover the happy path and the auth gate. The most security-sensitive code path — what happens with a malformed or missing `id` — is entirely untested. This makes it easy for the injection fix (once applied) to regress silently.

Suggested direction: Add test cases for: absent `id` query param, an `id` that fails `is_valid_id` (e.g., contains a quote), and a valid-format but non-existent `id` (expected 404).

---

## Nice to have

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData\Local\Temp\leverage-bench-2026-05-23_v0.10.0-cold-post-trim\T1__leveraged__r2\work\service\routes\users.py:8-9`** — Seed data committed inline in production route module

What: The `INSERT INTO users` seed statement lives in the route module rather than in a fixture or migration layer.

Why: Not a bug, but it blurs the boundary between application logic and test/seed data. `test_status.py` and `test_users.py` both use local `_Req` stubs, suggesting the project is moving toward isolated unit tests; having seed data in the module under test makes the database state implicit for anyone reading the tests.

Suggested direction: Move seed data to a test fixture or a dedicated `db.py` initialization helper, consistent with how other stateful setup would be handled as the service grows.
